content: The World Health Organization describes emergency care as integrated, time-sensitive care for acute illness and injury. This AI chatbot cannot examine a person or determine how serious symptoms are. For a possible emergency, contact the local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department immediately. This prototype is configured to mention 911 for the Philippines; verify the correct local number before any real-world use.
source: World Health Organization, Emergency and critical care, https://www.who.int/health-topics/emergency-care (accessed 2026-11-07)

content: Rehabilitation is a set of interventions designed to optimize functioning and reduce disability in people with health conditions, in interaction with their environment. It can help people of all ages be as independent as possible in everyday activities and participate in education, work, recreation, and family roles. Rehabilitation is person-centered: goals and services depend on a person's abilities, priorities, context, and assessment by qualified professionals. This information is educational and does not determine an individual's needs.

Rehabilitation may involve different professionals depending on a person's goals and health needs. A team can include physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech and language therapists, rehabilitation physicians, nurses, psychologists, and social workers. Not every person needs every profession, and services vary by setting. A qualified care team assesses needs, coordinates care, and agrees on relevant goals with the person. Rehabify Health is a fictional demo brand; this entry does not confirm that it employs or offers any listed service.
source: World Health Organization, Rehabilitation, https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rehabilitation (accessed 2026-11-07); fictional project note

content: Rehabilitation aims to support functioning and participation in activities that matter to the person. Goals are individual and can change over time as needs and abilities change. They should be discussed with the person and their qualified rehabilitation team after assessment. A chatbot cannot evaluate movement, pain, safety, progress, or readiness for an activity and should not set personal goals or prescribe exercises.

Assistive products can support functioning, independence, and participation. Examples include mobility aids, hearing aids, communication tools, and products that support vision or self-care. The right product depends on the person's needs and environment; selection, fitting, training, and follow-up may require qualified professionals. This general information is not a recommendation for a particular device, and this fictional project has no verified equipment or supply service.

A person's rehabilitation activities should be based on an assessment and plan from qualified professionals who understand their condition, abilities, environment, and risks. Do not start, stop, or intensify exercises based on chatbot advice. Stop an activity and contact the care team for individualized guidance if it causes new or worsening symptoms. Sudden severe symptoms, such as difficulty breathing, chest pain, or signs of stroke, need urgent medical attention rather than a rehabilitation chat.
source: General safety guidance for this educational prototype; individualized decisions require a qualified healthcare professional. Emergency care overview: World Health Organization, https://www.who.int/health-topics/emergency-care
